prompted_for: Documents delivered, as the package they audit (DocList as a turnover binder)
composition: light sentence-case headline on navy at top
limestone sheet with stacked-page edges behind
layout_devices: stacked paper offsets behind each folder
big mono index numbers per folder
small line icon top-right of each folder
page-reference footer line on each card
palette: steel-blue tab fills and one full folder
line_and_texture: ruler tick marks on sheet border
motion_implied: folders drop into the binder one by one
highlighted folder opens to its pages
t2i_keywords: limestone paper sheet on deep navy background
ruler tick marks on sheet border
t2i_prompt: Flat vector illustration of a documentation package: on a deep navy background, a large limestone sheet with ruler ticks on its edges and stacked page edges behind it. On the sheet, a neat grid of tabbed file folders drawn with 1.5 px navy outlines, each with offset sheets behind, a large mono index number, an uppercase mono title, a tiny line icon and a small footer line. Some tabs are steel-blue and one whole folder is filled steel-blue. Light grotesk headline above. <CONTENT>. Minimal shadow, calm archival feel.
signature_idea: The validation package shown as the physical binder of folders the auditor will open.
strengths: concrete, tactile metaphor for document turnover
weaknesses: folder cards are literal and skeuomorphic
rounded folder shapes break square corners
brand_fit_why: Colours and mono type fit, but skeuomorphic rounded folders and shadows read less precise than square drawing-sheet language.
